text.en: Asha's friend moved to a big city for her father's job. "Why do people move?" she asked.

Migration is the movement of people from one place to another to live. It may be internal, within a country, or international, between countries. It may be permanent or temporary and voluntary or forced.
Push factors drive people away, such as poverty, lack of jobs, drought or war. Pull factors attract them, such as jobs, better schools and safety. Rural to urban migration is common in India.
Migration brings remittances and skills but can cause crowded cities, slums and pressure on services. Migrant workers need protection and good living conditions.
Migration is the movement of people from one place to another to live.
It may be internal, within a country, or international, between countries.
It may be permanent or temporary and voluntary or forced.
Push factors drive people away, such as poverty, lack of jobs, drought or war.
Pull factors attract them, such as jobs, better schools and safety.
Rural to urban migration is common in India.
Migration brings remittances and skills but can cause crowded cities, slums and pressure on services.
Migrant workers need protection and good living conditions.
Let us measure how common migration is. According to census and survey findings, a very large share of India's and Tamil Nadu's population has moved at least once from their birthplace.

board.text: Migration is widespread across India & TN

text.en: Internal migration happens inside the same country and follows four streams: rural-to-rural, rural-to-urban, urban-to-urban, and urban-to-rural.
International migration crosses national borders. Many skilled and semi-skilled workers from Tamil Nadu work in Gulf countries, Singapore, Malaysia, Europe and North America.

Notice an important pattern in India's data: among female internal migrants, marriage is the most frequently recorded reason for changing residence, while among male migrants, work and employment dominate.
Let us contrast push and pull factors carefully. Push factors act at the place of origin: drought, tiny farm holdings, low wages, debt or conflict push families to leave.
Pull factors act at the destination: steady factory or IT jobs, higher wages, colleges, hospitals and safer transport pull newcomers in.
Seasonal or circular migrants move for a few months each year—for instance, to construction sites, brick kilns or sugarcane harvests—and then return home for planting season.
In Tamil Nadu, internal migration is strong toward industrial corridors like Chennai, Coimbatore, Tiruppur, Hosur and Erode, while coastal and southern districts send many workers abroad.
Migration reshapes the place of origin. On the positive side, money sent home—called remittances—helps families buy food, repair houses, repay debts and keep children in school.

board.text: Origin benefit: remittances boost family welfare

text.en: However, when too many young adults leave a village, elderly parents may lack daily care and local farms can face a shortage of skilled labour during harvest.

board.text: Origin challenge: labour shortage & elder care

text.en: When highly educated doctors, engineers or scientists move permanently abroad, economists call this brain drain. Yet if they invest back home or return with skills, it becomes brain gain.
Now look at the destination city. Migrants supply essential labour for factories, hospitals, metro construction, restaurants and software parks, driving urban GDP growth.
At the same time, rapid unplanned inflows can strain housing, clean drinking water, drainage, public buses and government schools, leading to overcrowded informal settlements.
Migrants sometimes face social barriers: language differences, lack of local ration cards, difficulty enrolling children in nearby schools, or unsafe worksites.
Policies like One Nation One Ration Card, portable health insurance, crèches at worksites and affordable rental housing help protect migrant workers' rights.
Strengthening rural jobs, agro-processing, cold storage and quality rural colleges reduces forced distress migration so people move by choice rather than desperation.
Education also changes the nature of migration: workers with higher education or vocational certificates are far more likely to find safe, well-paid formal jobs in cities or abroad.
Let us check a common misconception: migration is not only poor people moving to cities. Students moving for university and engineers moving between two metro cities are migrants too.
Another key distinction is emigration versus immigration: leaving one's home country is emigration, while entering a new country to live is immigration.
In geography and economics, urbanisation rises as the share of people living in towns and cities grows through both natural population growth and rural-to-urban migration.
To analyse any migration story, identify four items: the stream, the push factor, the pull factor, and one impact on both origin and destination.
Well-managed migration connects talent with opportunity while protecting human dignity at both the village left behind and the city welcoming newcomers.

problem.en: Karthik leaves a drought-hit village in Ramanathapuram to work in an automobile factory near Chennai and sends money home every month. Classify his migration and its effects.

text.en: Identify the migration stream.

why.en: Because he moved from a village to a city within Tamil Nadu, it is internal rural-to-urban migration.

text.en: Separate the push and pull factors.

why.en: Drought and lack of local income are push factors; steady factory wages near Chennai are the pull factor.

text.en: Note the economic effect on his village.

why.en: His monthly remittances raise his family's living standard and help fund education at home.

prompt.en: A friend says Migration happens only between countries. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: It can be within a country too.

points.en: It brings money but also problems.
